findings.title: Handle an empty destination-calendar list before checking its integration
findings.body: When a booking uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar, destructuring produces `undefined` and this condition dereferences `.integration`, throwing before the booking can be created. Check that the calendar exists before reading its integration.

findings.title: Select the Office 365 destination for the current credential
findings.body: EventManager invokes calendar creation once per destination, passing the matching credential ID, but this implementation ignores that ID and always uses the first destination calendar. For every later collective host, Graph is asked to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail with an access error or put the event in the wrong mailbox; the later host then receives no event.

findings.title: Select the Lark destination for the current credential
findings.body: EventManager invokes calendar creation once per destination, but this implementation always uses `event.destinationCalendar[0]` rather than the destination belonging to the credential being used. Later collective hosts therefore try to create their event in the first host's Lark calendar, typically failing due to permissions or creating it in the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Avoid filtering CalDAV creation to another host's calendar
findings.body: EventManager creates an event separately for each host credential, but this implementation filters the current account's calendars using only the first destination in the shared array. For a later host, that first calendar is generally not in their CalDAV account, so no event is created; the method can still return a successful result and leave a booking reference for an event that does not exist.

findings.title: Restore all collective destinations when confirming a booking
findings.body: This handler rebuilds the event using only the booking's single persisted destination calendar (or the current user's calendar). Collective host calendars are assembled during initial booking creation, but only one destination is stored on the booking, and this handler does not reload the other hosts' destinations. Confirming a pending collective booking therefore creates calendar events and references for at most one host, leaving the other hosts uninivited.

findings.title: Preserve collective destinations when creating paid-booking events
findings.body: On payment success this event contains only the booking's single persisted destination calendar or the organizer's calendar; it does not reload the collective hosts' destinations. When this path creates the calendar events, EventManager sees only one target, so other hosts are not invited. The setup-intent path in this file and the PayPal payment-success path have the same single-destination reconstruction and need the same fix.

findings.title: Use the destination calendar as the fallback for update and delete
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this `find` compares each calendar's external ID to that absent value, so it does not fall back to the event's destination calendar. Updates then receive an undefined calendar ID; deletes instead fall back to `primary` (the same broken lookup appears at line 317), which can leave the event on its selected calendar. This breaks operations for callers or older references without an external calendar ID.

findings.title: Delete every old calendar event when rescheduling to a new booking
findings.body: The reschedule update path now handles multiple calendar references, but when `newBookingId` is set this cleanup still finds and deletes only the first old calendar reference. Collective bookings can have an old event on each host's calendar, so the other hosts' old events remain after rescheduling and appear as duplicate appointments.

findings.title: Delete every host's event when cancelling a recurring collective booking
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch still selects only the first calendar reference for each updated booking and iterates only the booking user's credentials, rather than deleting each reference with its own credential. For collective bookings, events on secondary hosts' calendars are therefore left behind when cancelling the recurring series.

findings.title: Use each reference's credential when deleting events for a reschedule request
findings.body: Collective bookings can have several calendar references of the same integration type, each with its own `credentialId`, but this handler maps credentials only by integration type and uses that one credential for every reference. It can attempt to delete another host's event with the requester’s token; providers may reject the call or silently ignore a not-found response, leaving the old event on that host's calendar.
